### 25.4.12 source changes and released-package boundaries

- **Agent task fidelity and cutoff:** preserve original instructions and conditions, adding contextual facts rather than requirements. Official guidance describes at most three extra model calls on the same unexecuted cutoff turn, then the original error. Released templates retain older wording and the described reask loop is absent; this is not a permission boundary or positive recovery claim. See [core constraints](skills/ax-skills/references/agent.md#defaults-and-execution-constraints), [RLM stages](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#mental-model), [cutoff boundaries](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#actor-output-cutoff-versus-runtime-replay-truncation) and `32-executor-context/actor-cutoff-no-execution` in [32-executor-context.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/32-executor-context.ts).
- **Runtime analysis:** lightweight regex-literal recognition preserves completion/variable detection and division controls; it is not a full parser or sandbox proof. Live arithmetic/read values can differ from exported snapshots: the bounded postfix probe read `units: 25` while exporting `units: 24`. See [RLM actor rules](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#rlm-actor-code-rules) and `12-runtime/regex-completion-boundaries` / `12-runtime/division-state-boundaries` in [12-runtime.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/12-runtime.ts).
- **DeepSeek:** official guidance names `DeepSeekFlash` / `deepseek-flash` V4.1 as the text+image default, the old v4-flash server alias as deprecated, and retains V4-Pro. The released package instead has `DeepSeekV4Flash` / `deepseek-v4-flash` as default, no new enum or advertised native images, and function-only structured modes for exact native V4 rules when structured handling is needed. Ordinary singleton signatures need not select a structured rung; generic JSON-object fallback is capability-dependent, not a native DeepSeek guarantee. Matching released rules reject caller-forced tool choices; new-ID rules, server alias/image behavior and deployment equivalence are not established. See [DeepSeek boundaries](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#deepseek-notes) and amended `04-providers/deployment-reasoning-dialects` in [04-providers.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/04-providers.ts).
- **Events:** require actual non-whitespace strings for envelope `id`/`source`/`type` before routing or enqueue; valid values are not trimmed/coerced. This is neither authenticated identity nor generated-language runtime parity. See [event rules](skills/ax-skills/references/event-runtime.md#rules), [consumer checks](skills/ax-skills/references/event-runtime.md#testing) and `17-events/invalid-envelope-before-routing` in [17-events.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/17-events.ts).

The [25.4.11 release](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/releases/tag/25.4.11) remains a **retained historical baseline** for four related surfaces:

- **Streamed tool text:** preserve text accompanying tool calls, merge deltas and retain it in subsequent request history; see [generation](skills/ax-skills/references/gen.md#streaming-output-and-replacement-versions) and [03-tools-streaming.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/03-tools-streaming.ts). [PR 887](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/887) and [PR 891](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/891).
- **Gemini 4 Hydrogen:** apply its provider-specific thinking, request-size, schema/tool and streaming constraints, not generic Gemini assumptions; see [providers](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#gemini-4-hydrogen) and [04-providers.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/04-providers.ts). [PR 892](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/892).
- **Native document citations:** preserve source forms, URL-less document locations and passage associations. Replace streamed block snapshots rather than appending them; provenance is attribution, not truth. See [citations](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#anthropic-document-citations), [normalized logs](skills/ax-skills/references/gen.md#normalized-chat-logs-and-usage) and [37-document-citations.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/37-document-citations.ts). [PR 894](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/894), [PR 895](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/895) and [PR 896](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/896).
- **Shared references:** repeated sibling references are not ancestor cycles; preserve the former and mark only real cycles in executor replay. See [RLM](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#shared-references-are-not-cycles-25411) and [32-executor-context.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/32-executor-context.ts). [PR 893](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/893) and [PR 896](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/896).

The release/credit entries, including [PR 897](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/897), are organizational evidence, not extra APIs. Generated-language release notes establish source-described scope, not runtime qualification here. Dedicated Jev, OpenAI and Gemini Decisions remain distinct contracts; shared evidence shapes do not imply equivalent APIs or calibration. See [typed decisions](skills/ax-skills/references/typesafe.md).

Two bounded tsEpistle backports reconcile the MCP example and its index note: `29-mcp-oauth.ts` preserves an earlier operation error when its SSE listener also fails, while still surfacing an unexpected listener failure after successful operations; `examples/INDEX.md` describes that precedence instead of a throw from `finally`. A separate failure flag handles even `throw undefined`; host-owned close cancellation remains expected. This is error-precedence preservation, not broader transport reliability.

**Historical 25.4.9:** [PR 876](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/876) corrected empty-text Anthropic replay; [PR 883](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/883) aligned generated cache placement and plain unknown-tool errors; [PR 881](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/881) narrowed automatic setup. Those bounded contracts remain relevant, but their prior acceptance does not certify this revision.

Source API snapshot: `@ax-llm/ax` 25.4.12. Use for `contextMap` / `AxAgentContextMap`, memory catalogs/search/recall, `inputs.memories`, memory carryover and preloading, skill catalogs/search/discovery/preloading, loaded/used IDs and observers, and `relevanceRanking`. candidate_sections.heading: # AxAgent Observability
candidate_sections.text:
# AxAgent Observability

Use for AxAgent runtime visibility, progress, callbacks, telemetry, centralized or multi-tenant usage accounting, chat logs, and traces in `@ax-llm/ax`. Source API snapshot: 25.4.12. For setup see [agent authoring](agent.md); for runtime policy see [RLM](agent-rlm.md); for memories and dynamic skills see [memory and skills](agent-memory-skills.md). This is not general application logging.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Choose the smallest hook
candidate_sections.text:
## Choose the smallest hook

| Need | Surface |
| --- | --- |
| Development prompt/runtime trace | `debug: true` |
| Structured per-turn code, raw results, replay output, provider thoughts, actor stage | `actorTurnCallback` |
| Context pressure and compaction | `onContextEvent` |
| Actor-emitted real-time task progress | `agentStatusCallback` |
| Every JS runtime function call before execution | `onFunctionCall` |
| Model prompts/responses after a run | `getChatLog()` |
| Centralized chat/embedding usage across APIs, users, agents, services | `axGlobals.onUsage` with `usageContext` |
| Actor/responder token usage | `getUsage()`, `resetUsage()` |
| Context/task stage usage | `getStagedUsage()` |
| Ax program traces | `getTraces()` |

Add multiple hooks only when each output stream is needed. In particular, combine `debug: true` and `actorTurnCallback` only for both unstructured prompt/runtime visibility and structured telemetry. Do not scrape prompts or action logs when a callback exposes the data. Enable `showThoughts` only for needed provider-supported thought diagnostics; these are optional provider-returned fields, not guaranteed thoughts elicited by the callback.

### Direct respond (executor skip)

With `directResponse: 'auto'` (the default), the distiller can end the run with the `respond(task, evidence)` primitive when the task needs no executor authority — the executor stage is skipped entirely (zero executor model calls) and the responder synthesizes straight from the distiller's evidence. Unlike `final`, whose evidence stays live in the shared session by reference, `respond`'s evidence crosses into the responder prompt (budgeted by `maxEvidenceChars`), and the distiller's runtime variables are exported as the cross-run state exactly as the executor's would have been.

- **Static agents** (no functions, child agents, or native MCP/UCP operations) run respond-only: `final` is not offered to the distiller and every run is distiller → responder.
- **Agents with executor authority** from functions, child agents, or native MCP/UCP operations get `respond` alongside `final` under a conservative covenant: only for tasks answered purely by reading/synthesizing provided context, never when a listed function/module domain covers the need, never for current/live/fresh-state asks (context may be stale — tools are the source of truth for "now"), never for side effects. Landing-gate eval (both pinned models, 3 repeats): 0 false skips on tool-required tasks including a stale-context trap, 100% skip recall on pure context Q&A.
- `directResponse: 'off'` removes the primitive from the prompt and the runtime, and the pipeline rejects a respond payload outright.

Treat both actor stages as long-running code runtime sessions that the actor steers over multiple turns, not as fresh script generators on every turn. `AxJSRuntime` is the default; custom runtimes set `language` so the actor code field becomes `<language>Code` such as `pythonCode` while JavaScript keeps the legacy `javascriptCode`.

- Successful code leaves variables, functions, imports, and computed values available in the runtime session.
- The actor should continue from existing runtime state instead of recreating prior work.
- `actionLog`, `liveRuntimeState`, and checkpoint summaries only control what the actor can see again in the prompt.
- Rebuild state only after an explicit runtime restart notice or when you intentionally need to overwrite a value.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Mental Model
candidate_sections.text:
## Mental Model

`AxAgent` is a three-stage pipeline. Each `forward()` call walks the stages in order:

```text
distiller (RLM actor) -> executor (RLM actor) -> responder (synthesizer)
```

- **distiller** always runs first, with original inputs and runtime-only context fields. It gathers evidence through code, then calls `final(request, evidence)` to populate `inputs.executorRequest` and live evidence. Preserve the user's instructions and conditions in their original wording; add only contextual facts needed to resolve references or follow-ups such as “yes, do it.” Do not invent checks, steps, deliverables, reports or completion conditions. With no context fields, normalization still runs with `contextFields: []`. Metadata/skills discovery can be available, but external callable execution is blocked; the distiller is not a capability gate.
- **executor** receives non-context original inputs, `inputs.executorRequest`, a compact `distilledContextSummary` and live `inputs.distilledContext`. Declared/auto-promoted fields remain runtime-readable when listed by `contextMetadata`, not pasted in full into its prompt. When distillation adds or omits requirements, resolve the requested work against original task inputs. Execute only host-authorized actions and report actual tool outcomes; original user wording does not grant authority.
- **responder** always runs last. It synthesizes the user's output signature from whichever upstream actor finished the run and must not contradict tool evidence gathered upstream.

**Upstream guidance versus packaged templates:** the fidelity rules above come from [official RLM guidance](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/7db1c3b5a2a144b93b46cb649258bb52b26bd5a8/src/ax/skills/references/ax-agent-rlm.md). The supplied [25.4.12 source map](https://unpkg.com/@ax-llm/ax@25.4.12/index.js.map), `../agent/templates.generated.ts:8–9`, still bundles older wording: decoded distiller lines 9–11 say to “Expand” the task; decoded executor lines 7–15 prioritize distilled evidence. Neither template contains the new fidelity/precedence clauses. Handoff in `../agent/agentInternal/pipelineForward.ts:540–593` does not validate semantic equivalence or restore excluded fields. These are authoring rules, not runtime semantic enforcement or permission to treat untrusted context as instructions.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Use These Defaults
candidate_sections.text:
## Use These Defaults

- Use `agent(...)`, not `new AxAgent(...)`.
- In stdout-mode RLM, use one observable `console.log(...)` step per non-final actor turn.
- Rely on `autoUpgrade` (ON by default) for oversized inputs you did not declare in `contextFields`: any input value over ~8k serialized chars is kept runtime-only automatically, with a 1,200-char prompt preview plus a `contextMetadata` line, while the full value stays live in the runtime as `inputs.<field>`. Declare a field in `contextFields` only when you want a specific inline policy (`promptMaxChars` / `keepInPromptChars`) or need a large required non-string field kept out of the prompt (those are left inline by auto-upgrade).
- Choose replay, teaching detail, and model upgrades using [Prompt Level and Model Selection](#prompt-level-and-model-selection).
- Use `contextMap` for recurring long-context corpora when the distiller should start future runs with a small persisted orientation cache.
- Use explicit child agents in `functions: [...]` when the task needs specialist agents with their own tools/runtime.
- Use `llmQuery(...)` only for focused semantic questions over narrowed context; it does not spawn a tool-using child AxAgent.
- Prefer `maxSubAgentCalls` only when you need an explicit cap on `llmQuery(...)` sub-query usage.

## Choose the Agent Shape

| Need | Shape or companion reference |
| --- | --- |
| Use tools and answer | Plain `agent(...)` with local functions; minimal configuration, no extra observability |
| Delegate distinct specialist responsibilities | Child agents in `functions: [...]`; set each child's `agentIdentity.namespace` for call sites such as `team.writer(...)` |
| Discover unstable callable names or schemas | Enable discovery; generate discovery-first actor code |
| Let selected fatal errors escape the loop | `bubbleErrors` with Error classes; propagation covers function handlers, actor code, and `llmQuery(...)` sub-queries |
| Inspect large context with code, long-running execution, RLM, or `llmQuery(...)` | [RLM](agent-rlm.md); do not write a full multi-step RLM actor program in one turn |
| Callbacks, debugging, logs, traces, progress, tool/chat logs, or usage | [Agent observability](agent-observability.md) |
| Recall, dynamic memory/skill guides, `discover({ skills })`, loaded/used tracking | [Memory and runtime skills](agent-memory-skills.md) |
| `agent.optimize(...)`, tuning, evaluation, judge setup, datasets, saved artifacts | [Agent optimization](agent-optimize.md) |
| MCP clients, native modules, transports, authentication, catalogs, subscriptions, tasks, Apps, server handlers, recording/replay, or event-driven wake/resume | [MCP](mcp.md); [event runtime](event-runtime.md) covers wake/resume orchestration |

## Host-Side Completion and Unified Final Signal
### Payload constraints
candidate_sections.text:
### Payload constraints

String shorthand is valid: `askClarification("What dates should I use?")`. Prefer structured payloads for richer UIs:

```javascript
askClarification({
  question: 'Which route should I use?',
  type: 'single_choice',
  choices: ['Fastest', 'Scenic'],
});
```

- Supported `type`: `text`, `number`, `date`, `single_choice`, `multiple_choice`.
- Choice entries are strings or `{ label, value? }` objects.
- Missing, empty, or malformed `single_choice.choices` downgrades to a plain clarification question instead of failing the turn.
- `multiple_choice` requires at least two valid choices; otherwise the actor turn fails with a corrective runtime error.
- Invalid payloads, such as a missing `question`, are actor-turn runtime errors, not successful clarification completions.

candidate_sections.heading: ## DeepSeek Notes
candidate_sections.text:
## DeepSeek Notes

```typescript
import { ai, AxAIDeepSeekModel } from '@ax-llm/ax';

const deepseek = ai({
  name: 'deepseek',
  apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_APIKEY!,
  // Released 25.4.12 enum/default; see the official-source mismatch below.
  config: { model: AxAIDeepSeekModel.DeepSeekV4Flash },
});
```

The supplied official 25.4.12 provider guidance (“DeepSeek Notes”) names `AxAIDeepSeekModel.DeepSeekFlash` / `deepseek-flash` (V4.1-Flash) as the default with text and image input, alongside `deepseek-v4-pro`. It says V4-Flash retired on 2026-09-10 and `deepseek-v4-flash` is now a server alias, deprecated in Ax.

**Released-package mismatch:** the supplied 25.4.12 declarations have no `DeepSeekFlash` member; its catalog/profile still defaults to `DeepSeekV4Flash` / `deepseek-v4-flash`, without a deprecation annotation on that member, a `deepseek-flash` rule, or advertised DeepSeek image support. The runnable example above deliberately uses the released enum. Do not invent an enum alias, model-info override, or image-success fixture to bridge this gap. Generic OpenAI image serialization does not establish DeepSeek image support; server alias behavior and image understanding are not verified here. Legacy enum/catalog values remain available, but model rules belong to the selected deployment.

For the released native Chat profile's exact V4 Flash/Pro IDs, omitted `thinkingTokenBudget` selects logical `max`: `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` and `reasoning_effort: "max"`. Explicit `none` sends disabled thinking and omits effort. `minimal`/`low` map to `low`, `medium` and `high` are preserved, and `highest`/`xhigh`/`max` map to `max`. Enabled thinking removes incompatible sampling parameters. Do not generalize this V4 mapping to every legacy alias.

The released native rules omit auto and Ax-generated `__axOutput` tool choices for `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, and `deepseek-reasoner`, while retaining tool definitions. Caller `required` or named forced choices fail before transport, including a caller naming `__axOutput`; `none` removes tools as well. Official guidance adds `deepseek-flash` to this list, but that ID has no matching rule in the supplied release. DeepSeek Responses is a separate profile, not evidence of native Chat dialect parity.

Structured-output selection is capability-gated, not a blanket singleton promise. Native JSON Schema is unsupported; the released native V4/Reasoner rules advertise **function-only** structured output, so auto selection uses synthetic `__axOutput` when structured handling is needed. Ordinary non-complex signatures need not select any structured rung. A single required `string`/`code` can use validated `json_object` without provider tools only when structured handling is selected **and** the model advertises that mode; the official singleton wording (including actor `javascriptCode`) does not establish it for these released native rules. See [structured-rungs and singleton-json-fallback](../examples/02-generation.ts) for generic capability-dependent parsing, not DeepSeek model support.

DeepSeek Chat returns thinking traces as `reasoning_content`. During a tool loop, Ax preserves that field on the assistant tool-call message and sends it back on the following request together with non-null `content` and the original tool calls. This compatibility mode is declared by the DeepSeek deployment profile; the official OpenAI Chat adapter does not emit or expose `reasoning_content`.

The same logical default is declared independently for verified DeepSeek V4 rules in Together, Fireworks, and OpenRouter, then mapped to each deployment's own dialect: Together uses `reasoning_effort` without native `thinking`, OpenRouter uses nested `reasoning`, and Fireworks uses its own effort mapping. Keep hosted model IDs unchanged; native model names or server aliases do not confer hosted capabilities or pricing. A custom `openai-compatible` endpoint never inherits reasoning rules from a DeepSeek-looking model ID. The [deployment-reasoning-dialects case](../examples/04-providers.ts) checks the released native default, actual pre-transport rejection, and native/Together/custom wire distinctions with injected HTTP, not live provider quality or generated-language parity.

Other verified deployment rules follow the same policy. Grok 4.6 maps logical `max` to `xhigh`, while Grok 4.5 and 4.3 map it to `high`. Groq GPT-OSS and Cerebras GPT-OSS map it to `high`; Groq Qwen 3.6 maps it to its documented reasoning-enabled `default`; Cerebras Gemma 4 and DeepInfra DeepSeek R1 map it to `high`. An explicit `none` is sent only for model/deployment combinations that document disabling reasoning. Grok 4.6/4.5 and GPT-OSS on Groq or Cerebras reject `none` before network I/O because those APIs do not support disabling reasoning for those models.

Hugging Face Router remains conservative: routing policies such as `:fastest` may choose a different inference provider without changing the base model ID, so Ax does not attach one provider's reasoning contract to that dynamic route.

candidate_sections.heading: ## AWS Bedrock
### Anthropic Model-Specific Behavior
candidate_sections.text:
### Anthropic Model-Specific Behavior

- Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, 4.7, and 4.6 plus Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5:
  adaptive thinking, no manual `budget_tokens`, and no `temperature` / `topP` /
  `topK`. When thoughts are requested, Ax asks Anthropic for summarized
  display; when they are hidden, Ax explicitly requests `display: 'omitted'`.
- Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5 always think, so `thinkingTokenBudget:
  'none'` sends the lowest effort with thoughts hidden instead of disabling it.
- Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 think by default, so `'none'` sends
  `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }`. Opus 5 only allows that at effort `'high'`
  or below, so Ax rejects `'none'` combined with `'xhigh'` or `'max'`.
- Sonnet 5.5 uses `thinking: { type: 'between_tools' }` for `'none'`,
  allowed at effort `'high'` or below. Its signed between-tool updates are
  retained in `thoughtBlocks` for replay even when display thoughts are hidden.
  Streaming and non-streaming responses preserve both thinking and redacted
  blocks; `showThoughts: false` suppresses the display `thought` field.
  The generated Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust clients share these rules,
  including effort validation, native structured output, and signed replay.
- Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1 refuse forced tool choice: Ax throws for
  `functionCall: 'required'` or a named function, and structured output uses
  the native `output_config.format` path.
- Haiku 5.5 (`AxAIAnthropicModel.Claude55Haiku`, also on Vertex):
  adaptive thinking defaults to medium effort. `'none'` sends
  `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }`; combining it with `'xhigh'` or `'max'`
  fails locally. Other thinking levels use adaptive thinking with effort.
  Forced tool choice is supported, as are native JSON Schema and function-based
  structured outputs. Empty signed thinking blocks remain available for replay;
  keep history append-only, including later system messages on both APIs.
  The context window is 1M tokens and the output limit is 128K. Per million
  tokens, input/output pricing is $0.10/$0.50 through 100K input tokens and
  $0.50/$2.50 above 100K, counting cached input toward the threshold. Cache
  reads and 5-minute writes use the corresponding tier. These semantics are
  shared with the generated Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust packages.
- Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5, and Fable 5.1 keep a later system
  message in place on the first-party API; other models hoist it into the
  system prompt. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 preserve later system messages on Vertex,
  keeping the prefix before signed thinking unchanged.
- Opus 4.5: budget_tokens + effort levels (capped at `'high'`)
- Other thinking models: budget tokens only

For assistant replay, empty visible text (`content: ''`) adds no synthetic text block. Cache markers attach only to text or tool-use blocks, never to signed or redacted thinking. See the [25.4.9 replay mapper](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/3ad7b69947e05f1770b1bd6cb1316a8ec7fcd106/src/ax/ai/anthropic/api.ts#L1871-L2013).

Anthropic `modelConfig.effort` can be set directly on a request. Fast mode and task budgets are Anthropic-only opt-ins; `taskBudget.total` must be at least 20,000 tokens.

```typescript
const res = await claude.chat({
  chatPrompt: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Review this migration plan.' }],
  modelConfig: {
    effort: 'xhigh',
    speed: 'fast',
    taskBudget: { type: 'tokens', total: 64_000 },
  },
});
```

candidate_sections.heading: ## Rules
candidate_sections.text:
## Rules

- Supply identity from authenticated adapter state, never from event data.
- Treat events without verified identity as anonymous and untrusted.
- Envelope `id`, `source`, and `type` must each be a primitive string containing
  a non-whitespace character. TypeScript rejects malformed fields before route
  matching or store enqueue, not as mapped-input dead letters. It validates
  without trimming or coercing accepted values. These envelope identifiers are
  distinct from authenticated `AxEventIdentity` fields such as `tenantId`;
  nonblank identifiers do not establish authority or URI validity.
- Map event data into signature inputs; do not synthesize a user message.
- Use `eventPath.data('field')` and other segment-safe selectors. Do not use
  dotted JSONPath strings or repurpose `s()` as a mapping language.
- Use `.project(path)` only for same-name signature projection. Explicit
  `.field()` mappings override projection; missing or invalid signature inputs
  dead-letter before model invocation.
- Use `eventInput().project(...).field(...)` when a declarative mapping should
  be callback-free and reusable, then pass that plan to `.input()`,
  `.wakeInput()`, or `.resumeInput()`.
- Callback `mapInput` is an escape hatch, not a validation bypass: its result is
  normalized to the program signature and mapper failures dead-letter before
  invocation.
- Use `.wakeInput()` and `.resumeInput()` when the two actions need different
  contracts. Neither action silently uses the other action's mapping.
- Use `observe` for progress/logs and `invalidate` for catalog changes.
- Use `resume` only with an owned continuation correlation key.
- Use `.createProgram(signature, factory)` for fresh, state-restorable instances of stateful multi-tenant Agents; do not share one mutable instance across tenants.
- Declare `retrySafety: 'idempotent'` only when stable delivery keys protect
  every possible side effect.
- Persist outputs before final sink delivery; redrive sink failures separately.
- Use `debounceMs` and `coalesce: 'latest'` only when replacing intermediate
  events is part of the route's declared policy.
- Observe source failures with `onSourceError`.
- The in-memory store is volatile and single-process.
- For cooperating Node processes on one local disk, use
  `AxSQLiteEventStore` from `@ax-llm/ax-tools/event/sqlite` with explicit
  retention and `coordination: 'multi-worker'`. Never recommend SQLite on a
  network filesystem.
- Close the runtime and caller-owned protocol clients explicitly.
- Fan out to several Agents with several matching routes, not a multi-target
  route. This preserves independent authorization, ordering, retries, and runs.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Minimal Pattern
## UCP Adapter
candidate_sections.text:
## UCP Adapter

Use `AxUCPWebhookEventSource({ client, identity })` inside an application-owned
HTTP handler, then call `source.ingest(request)`. The client verifies signer
profile, RFC 9421 signature, digest, freshness and key rotation before enqueue.
Resolve tenant/account identity from trusted application registration after
verification; never copy authority from the business payload.

**25.4.11 replay qualification:** `AxUCPClient.verifyOrderEvent` creates a new
signature verifier per request; its persistent process-local replay check uses
`Webhook-Id`, while that header and `Webhook-Timestamp` need not be signed.
Bind them to the signed `request-id` and `created` before ingestion, and require
the signed signer-profile header. Parse exactly one verified signature member
with unique parameters; bind metadata to that member, not a separately selected
or ambiguous `Signature-Input` entry. The
[`35-ucp/webhook-freshness-member-binding`](../examples/35-ucp.ts) case includes a
fresh `created`-last control and rejects old or ambiguous metadata before enqueue.
The [verified webhook example](../examples/35-ucp.ts) also covers real client
verification, key rotation, tamper/replay rejection and host-bound tenant routing.
Its volatile replay state is not restart durability; production hosts need
durable replay/idempotency policy. Source:
[`25.4.11 client and signing code`](https://unpkg.com/@ax-llm/ax@25.4.11/index.js.map),
embedded `../ucp/client.ts` (`verifyOrderEvent`) and `../ucp/signing.ts`.

Native UCP attachment is independent of transport. The same example carries
UCP through Flow → Agent/Gen and preserves structured results; MCP-backed UCP
also reuses protocol sessions and propagates cancellation. Attaching a client
does not itself authorize purchases or establish tenant isolation.

The generated-language statements below describe the supplied source's scope, not runtime qualification performed by this collection.

The supplied official 25.4.12 event-runtime guidance
also specifies field-specific `id`/`source`/`type` validation before routing or
enqueue in generated runtimes; Python dictionary envelope fields are not
string-coerced. This is source-only guidance, not independently exercised
generated/Python runtime parity. The TypeScript case below exercises the
released TypeScript boundary only.

Generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust packages expose the same Core-owned
single-worker event state machine plus functioning inline lifecycle dispatch,
continuations, state restoration, cancellation, persisted outputs, isolated
sink redrive, signature-aware path/input/target/route builders, and host-owned
source, sink, clock, and store boundaries. Generated targets use the host
signature plus a typed invocation callback when no common object-safe program
interface exists. Do not claim persistent multi-worker support from
`axevent.single-worker` alone.

Generated runtimes do not create worker threads. `publish()` drains work due at
`clock.now()`. Hosts use `nextDueAt()` to schedule `runDue()` for debounce,
retry, and continuation expiry; `redrive()` is due immediately. Manual clocks
make these transitions deterministic. Generated in-memory stores enforce
10,000 pending deliveries, 64 MiB queued data, 1 MiB per envelope, and a
five-second publication wait.

System and manual clock sleeps accept the generated cancellation token (Go uses
`context.Context`). Cancellation wakes the sleep without advancing a manual
clock, preserves the token's first reason, and removes its wake subscription on
both cancellation and normal completion. Repeated completed sleeps must not
retain timers, callbacks, condition registrations, or manual-clock waiters.

## Builder rules and boundaries
candidate_sections.text:
## Builder rules and boundaries

- Import `import { ai, flow, f } from '@ax-llm/ax';`; use the `flow()` factory, never `new AxFlow(...)` for new code.
- Define each `.node()` before its `.execute()`; reversed order throws. `.execute()` maps current state to node inputs; `.map()` shapes state without AI calls; `.returns()` maps final state to the output contract.
- Use `flow<InputType, OutputType>()` and explicit input/output generics; do not infer broad signatures from arbitrary transform source. Finish execution steps with `.returns()` or `.r()` to lock output type. Removed terminal shapers `.mapOutput()` and `.mo()` must not be used.
- Keep state flat; do not create deeply nested objects in `.map()`. Use descriptive node names (`documentSummarizer`, not `proc1`) and field names (`userInput`, `responseText`, not generic `text`, `result`, `data`, `input`, `output`).
- Independent executes and derives safely auto-parallelize by default when metadata reads/writes are known and non-conflicting. Do not add unnecessary execute dependencies. Conditions must change; feedback needs a maximum-iteration guard. Access untaken branch results with optional chaining after `.merge()`.
- Aliases: `.n()` = `.node()`, `.nx()` = `.nodeExtended()`, `.m()` = `.map()`, `.r()` = `.returns()`.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Execution and selection contract
candidate_sections.text:
## Execution and selection contract

- Use `optimize(program, train, metric, { studentAI, teacherAI, ... })` for normal generator/flow tuning; prefer `ai()`, `ax()`, and `flow()` for new code. Choose a cheaper student and strong teacher.
- Both `optimize(...)` and `AxGEPA.compile()` support a single generator or a tree-aware root (flow/agent) with registered optimizable descendants. There is no flow-only GEPA optimizer.
- GEPA edits generic string components from `getOptimizableComponents()`; a tree exposing none fails. Register child programs under the root. Selection uses measured component accept/reject history, not LLM-generated numeric scores: the teacher proposes text, metrics decide acceptance.
- With at most eight training examples, global `optimize(...)` defaults to `AxBootstrapFewShot -> AxGEPA`, retaining demos in `result.optimizedProgram.demos`; override with `bootstrap: false` or explicit bootstrap options. Direct `AxGEPA` has its own `bootstrap` option instead.
- Always keep `train` and held-out `validationExamples` distinct; do not reuse training examples for selection. Pass a holdout when available.
- Set `maxMetricCalls` to bound GEPA evaluations, not total provider calls. Global `optimize(...)` uses at least `100` implicitly, increasing it only to fit mandatory validation passes; it never raises an explicit limit. Direct `AxGEPA.compile()` requires a positive limit. Reserve validation plus evolution rounds; for expensive trees start with `auto: 'light'` or fewer `numTrials`, then scale up.
- `result.optimizedProgram` is the best easy-to-apply candidate; `result.paretoFront` is the complete multi-objective trade-off set. Apply with `program.applyOptimization(result.optimizedProgram!)`, not only `setInstruction(...)`.
- Function/tool trace reflection uses stable component IDs where available; function renames do not break saved candidate maps.

### 25.4.12 source changes and released-package boundaries

- **Agent task fidelity and cutoff:** preserve original instructions and conditions, adding contextual facts rather than requirements. Official guidance describes at most three extra model calls on the same unexecuted cutoff turn, then the original error. Released templates retain older wording and the described reask loop is absent; this is not a permission boundary or positive recovery claim. See [core constraints](skills/ax-skills/references/agent.md#defaults-and-execution-constraints), [RLM stages](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#mental-model), [cutoff boundaries](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#actor-output-cutoff-versus-runtime-replay-truncation) and `32-executor-context/actor-cutoff-no-execution` in [32-executor-context.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/32-executor-context.ts).
- **Runtime analysis:** lightweight regex-literal recognition preserves completion/variable detection and division controls; it is not a full parser or sandbox proof. Live arithmetic/read values can differ from exported snapshots: the bounded postfix probe read `units: 25` while exporting `units: 24`. See [RLM actor rules](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#rlm-actor-code-rules) and `12-runtime/regex-completion-boundaries` / `12-runtime/division-state-boundaries` in [12-runtime.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/12-runtime.ts).
- **DeepSeek:** official guidance names `DeepSeekFlash` / `deepseek-flash` V4.1 as the text+image default, the old v4-flash server alias as deprecated, and retains V4-Pro. The released package instead has `DeepSeekV4Flash` / `deepseek-v4-flash` as default, no new enum or advertised native images, and function-only structured modes for exact native V4 rules when structured handling is needed. Ordinary singleton signatures need not select a structured rung; generic JSON-object fallback is capability-dependent, not a native DeepSeek guarantee. Matching released rules reject caller-forced tool choices; new-ID rules, server alias/image behavior and deployment equivalence are not established. See [DeepSeek boundaries](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#deepseek-notes) and amended `04-providers/deployment-reasoning-dialects` in [04-providers.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/04-providers.ts).
- **Events:** require actual non-whitespace strings for envelope `id`/`source`/`type` before routing or enqueue; valid values are not trimmed/coerced. This is neither authenticated identity nor generated-language runtime parity. See [event rules](skills/ax-skills/references/event-runtime.md#rules), [consumer checks](skills/ax-skills/references/event-runtime.md#testing) and `17-events/invalid-envelope-before-routing` in [17-events.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/17-events.ts).

The [25.4.11 release](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/releases/tag/25.4.11) remains a **retained historical baseline** for four related surfaces:

- **Streamed tool text:** preserve text accompanying tool calls, merge deltas and retain it in subsequent request history; see [generation](skills/ax-skills/references/gen.md#streaming-output-and-replacement-versions) and [03-tools-streaming.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/03-tools-streaming.ts). [PR 887](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/887) and [PR 891](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/891).
- **Gemini 4 Hydrogen:** apply its provider-specific thinking, request-size, schema/tool and streaming constraints, not generic Gemini assumptions; see [providers](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#gemini-4-hydrogen) and [04-providers.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/04-providers.ts). [PR 892](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/892).
- **Native document citations:** preserve source forms, URL-less document locations and passage associations. Replace streamed block snapshots rather than appending them; provenance is attribution, not truth. See [citations](skills/ax-skills/references/ai.md#anthropic-document-citations), [normalized logs](skills/ax-skills/references/gen.md#normalized-chat-logs-and-usage) and [37-document-citations.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/37-document-citations.ts). [PR 894](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/894), [PR 895](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/895) and [PR 896](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/896).
- **Shared references:** repeated sibling references are not ancestor cycles; preserve the former and mark only real cycles in executor replay. See [RLM](skills/ax-skills/references/agent-rlm.md#shared-references-are-not-cycles-25411) and [32-executor-context.ts](skills/ax-skills/examples/32-executor-context.ts). [PR 893](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/893) and [PR 896](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/896).

The release/credit entries, including [PR 897](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/897), are organizational evidence, not extra APIs. Generated-language release notes establish source-described scope, not runtime qualification here. Dedicated Jev, OpenAI and Gemini Decisions remain distinct contracts; shared evidence shapes do not imply equivalent APIs or calibration. See [typed decisions](skills/ax-skills/references/typesafe.md).

Two bounded tsEpistle backports reconcile the MCP example and its index note: `29-mcp-oauth.ts` preserves an earlier operation error when its SSE listener also fails, while still surfacing an unexpected listener failure after successful operations; `examples/INDEX.md` describes that precedence instead of a throw from `finally`. A separate failure flag handles even `throw undefined`; host-owned close cancellation remains expected. This is error-precedence preservation, not broader transport reliability.

**Historical 25.4.9:** [PR 876](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/876) corrected empty-text Anthropic replay; [PR 883](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/883) aligned generated cache placement and plain unknown-tool errors; [PR 881](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/881) narrowed automatic setup. Those bounded contracts remain relevant, but their prior acceptance does not certify this revision.

## Working policy

1. **Design, mechanism selection, or cross-language porting:** read [Architecture](references/architecture.md) first, even for a single subsystem such as retrieval, image localization or audio routing. Then load only the selected specialist sections and relevant example. **Narrow coding or debugging:** go directly to the owning row below. Do not preload every guide or the example corpus.
2. Prefer `ai()`, `ax()`, `agent()`, `flow()`, `optimize()`, `s()`, `f()` and `fn()` where supported; use specialized classes when required.
3. This collection integrates official `@ax-llm/ax` **25.4.12 guidance** plus authored design synthesis, not universal released-package support. The pinned TypeScript SDK lacks the described actor-cutoff reasks and new fidelity-template wording; DeepSeek retains the old enum/default, no advertised images and capability-gated, function-only native V4 structured mode. Owning guides distinguish source intent from implementation. Check installed declarations; do not infer generated-language parity.
4. Keep credentials in application environment/secret storage, never examples or logs. Before verification inspect scripts and obtain task-required authorization. Prefer local type checks and focused tests; never silently run billed model calls, external services, live audio or state-changing operations. Report only checks actually exercised.

candidate_sections.text:
### Direct respond (executor skip)

With `directResponse: 'auto'` (the default), the distiller can end the run with the `respond(task, evidence)` primitive when the task needs no executor authority — the executor stage is skipped entirely (zero executor model calls) and the responder synthesizes straight from the distiller's evidence. Unlike `final`, whose evidence stays live in the shared session by reference, `respond`'s evidence crosses into the responder prompt (budgeted by `maxEvidenceChars`), and the distiller's runtime variables are exported as the cross-run state exactly as the executor's would have been.

- **Static agents** (no functions, child agents, or native MCP/UCP operations) run respond-only: `final` is not offered to the distiller and every run is distiller → responder.
- **Agents with executor authority** from functions, child agents, or native MCP/UCP operations get `respond` alongside `final` under a conservative covenant: only for tasks answered purely by reading/synthesizing provided context, never when a listed function/module domain covers the need, never for current/live/fresh-state asks (context may be stale — tools are the source of truth for "now"), never for side effects. Landing-gate eval (both pinned models, 3 repeats): 0 false skips on tool-required tasks including a stale-context trap, 100% skip recall on pure context Q&A.
- `directResponse: 'off'` removes the primitive from the prompt and the runtime, and the pipeline rejects a respond payload outright.

Treat both actor stages as long-running code runtime sessions that the actor steers over multiple turns, not as fresh script generators on every turn. `AxJSRuntime` is the default; custom runtimes set `language` so the actor code field becomes `<language>Code` such as `pythonCode` while JavaScript keeps the legacy `javascriptCode`.

- Successful code leaves variables, functions, imports, and computed values available in the runtime session.
- The actor should continue from existing runtime state instead of recreating prior work.
- `actionLog`, `liveRuntimeState`, and checkpoint summaries only control what the actor can see again in the prompt.
- Rebuild state only after an explicit runtime restart notice or when you intentionally need to overwrite a value.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Mental Model
candidate_sections.text:
## Mental Model

`AxAgent` is a three-stage pipeline. Each `forward()` call walks the stages in order:

```text
distiller (RLM actor) -> executor (RLM actor) -> responder (synthesizer)
```

- **distiller** always runs first, with original inputs and runtime-only context fields. It gathers evidence through code, then calls `final(request, evidence)` to populate `inputs.executorRequest` and live evidence. Preserve the user's instructions and conditions in their original wording; add only contextual facts needed to resolve references or follow-ups such as “yes, do it.” Do not invent checks, steps, deliverables, reports or completion conditions. With no context fields, normalization still runs with `contextFields: []`. Metadata/skills discovery can be available, but external callable execution is blocked; the distiller is not a capability gate.
- **executor** receives non-context original inputs, `inputs.executorRequest`, a compact `distilledContextSummary` and live `inputs.distilledContext`. Declared/auto-promoted fields remain runtime-readable when listed by `contextMetadata`, not pasted in full into its prompt. When distillation adds or omits requirements, resolve the requested work against original task inputs. Execute only host-authorized actions and report actual tool outcomes; original user wording does not grant authority.
- **responder** always runs last. It synthesizes the user's output signature from whichever upstream actor finished the run and must not contradict tool evidence gathered upstream.

**Upstream guidance versus packaged templates:** the fidelity rules above come from [official RLM guidance](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/7db1c3b5a2a144b93b46cb649258bb52b26bd5a8/src/ax/skills/references/ax-agent-rlm.md). The supplied [25.4.12 source map](https://unpkg.com/@ax-llm/ax@25.4.12/index.js.map), `../agent/templates.generated.ts:8–9`, still bundles older wording: decoded distiller lines 9–11 say to “Expand” the task; decoded executor lines 7–15 prioritize distilled evidence. Neither template contains the new fidelity/precedence clauses. Handoff in `../agent/agentInternal/pipelineForward.ts:540–593` does not validate semantic equivalence or restore excluded fields. These are authoring rules, not runtime semantic enforcement or permission to treat untrusted context as instructions.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Use These Defaults
candidate_sections.text:
## Use These Defaults

- Use `agent(...)`, not `new AxAgent(...)`.
- In stdout-mode RLM, use one observable `console.log(...)` step per non-final actor turn.
- Rely on `autoUpgrade` (ON by default) for oversized inputs you did not declare in `contextFields`: any input value over ~8k serialized chars is kept runtime-only automatically, with a 1,200-char prompt preview plus a `contextMetadata` line, while the full value stays live in the runtime as `inputs.<field>`. Declare a field in `contextFields` only when you want a specific inline policy (`promptMaxChars` / `keepInPromptChars`) or need a large required non-string field kept out of the prompt (those are left inline by auto-upgrade).
- Choose replay, teaching detail, and model upgrades using [Prompt Level and Model Selection](#prompt-level-and-model-selection).
- Use `contextMap` for recurring long-context corpora when the distiller should start future runs with a small persisted orientation cache.
- Use explicit child agents in `functions: [...]` when the task needs specialist agents with their own tools/runtime.
- Use `llmQuery(...)` only for focused semantic questions over narrowed context; it does not spawn a tool-using child AxAgent.
- Prefer `maxSubAgentCalls` only when you need an explicit cap on `llmQuery(...)` sub-query usage.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Clarification and Resume State
## Host-Side Completion and Unified Final Signal
### Payload constraints
candidate_sections.text:
### Payload constraints

String shorthand is valid: `askClarification("What dates should I use?")`. Prefer structured payloads for richer UIs:

```javascript
askClarification({
  question: 'Which route should I use?',
  type: 'single_choice',
  choices: ['Fastest', 'Scenic'],
});
```

- Supported `type`: `text`, `number`, `date`, `single_choice`, `multiple_choice`.
- Choice entries are strings or `{ label, value? }` objects.
- Missing, empty, or malformed `single_choice.choices` downgrades to a plain clarification question instead of failing the turn.
- `multiple_choice` requires at least two valid choices; otherwise the actor turn fails with a corrective runtime error.
- Invalid payloads, such as a missing `question`, are actor-turn runtime errors, not successful clarification completions.

candidate_sections.heading: ## DeepSeek Notes
candidate_sections.text:
## DeepSeek Notes

```typescript
import { ai, AxAIDeepSeekModel } from '@ax-llm/ax';

const deepseek = ai({
  name: 'deepseek',
  apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_APIKEY!,
  // Released 25.4.12 enum/default; see the official-source mismatch below.
  config: { model: AxAIDeepSeekModel.DeepSeekV4Flash },
});
```

The supplied official 25.4.12 provider guidance (“DeepSeek Notes”) names `AxAIDeepSeekModel.DeepSeekFlash` / `deepseek-flash` (V4.1-Flash) as the default with text and image input, alongside `deepseek-v4-pro`. It says V4-Flash retired on 2026-09-10 and `deepseek-v4-flash` is now a server alias, deprecated in Ax.

**Released-package mismatch:** the supplied 25.4.12 declarations have no `DeepSeekFlash` member; its catalog/profile still defaults to `DeepSeekV4Flash` / `deepseek-v4-flash`, without a deprecation annotation on that member, a `deepseek-flash` rule, or advertised DeepSeek image support. The runnable example above deliberately uses the released enum. Do not invent an enum alias, model-info override, or image-success fixture to bridge this gap. Generic OpenAI image serialization does not establish DeepSeek image support; server alias behavior and image understanding are not verified here. Legacy enum/catalog values remain available, but model rules belong to the selected deployment.

For the released native Chat profile's exact V4 Flash/Pro IDs, omitted `thinkingTokenBudget` selects logical `max`: `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` and `reasoning_effort: "max"`. Explicit `none` sends disabled thinking and omits effort. `minimal`/`low` map to `low`, `medium` and `high` are preserved, and `highest`/`xhigh`/`max` map to `max`. Enabled thinking removes incompatible sampling parameters. Do not generalize this V4 mapping to every legacy alias.

The released native rules omit auto and Ax-generated `__axOutput` tool choices for `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, and `deepseek-reasoner`, while retaining tool definitions. Caller `required` or named forced choices fail before transport, including a caller naming `__axOutput`; `none` removes tools as well. Official guidance adds `deepseek-flash` to this list, but that ID has no matching rule in the supplied release. DeepSeek Responses is a separate profile, not evidence of native Chat dialect parity.

Structured-output selection is capability-gated, not a blanket singleton promise. Native JSON Schema is unsupported; the released native V4/Reasoner rules advertise **function-only** structured output, so auto selection uses synthetic `__axOutput` when structured handling is needed. Ordinary non-complex signatures need not select any structured rung. A single required `string`/`code` can use validated `json_object` without provider tools only when structured handling is selected **and** the model advertises that mode; the official singleton wording (including actor `javascriptCode`) does not establish it for these released native rules. See [structured-rungs and singleton-json-fallback](../examples/02-generation.ts) for generic capability-dependent parsing, not DeepSeek model support.

DeepSeek Chat returns thinking traces as `reasoning_content`. During a tool loop, Ax preserves that field on the assistant tool-call message and sends it back on the following request together with non-null `content` and the original tool calls. This compatibility mode is declared by the DeepSeek deployment profile; the official OpenAI Chat adapter does not emit or expose `reasoning_content`.

The same logical default is declared independently for verified DeepSeek V4 rules in Together, Fireworks, and OpenRouter, then mapped to each deployment's own dialect: Together uses `reasoning_effort` without native `thinking`, OpenRouter uses nested `reasoning`, and Fireworks uses its own effort mapping. Keep hosted model IDs unchanged; native model names or server aliases do not confer hosted capabilities or pricing. A custom `openai-compatible` endpoint never inherits reasoning rules from a DeepSeek-looking model ID. The [deployment-reasoning-dialects case](../examples/04-providers.ts) checks the released native default, actual pre-transport rejection, and native/Together/custom wire distinctions with injected HTTP, not live provider quality or generated-language parity.

Other verified deployment rules follow the same policy. Grok 4.6 maps logical `max` to `xhigh`, while Grok 4.5 and 4.3 map it to `high`. Groq GPT-OSS and Cerebras GPT-OSS map it to `high`; Groq Qwen 3.6 maps it to its documented reasoning-enabled `default`; Cerebras Gemma 4 and DeepInfra DeepSeek R1 map it to `high`. An explicit `none` is sent only for model/deployment combinations that document disabling reasoning. Grok 4.6/4.5 and GPT-OSS on Groq or Cerebras reject `none` before network I/O because those APIs do not support disabling reasoning for those models.

Hugging Face Router remains conservative: routing policies such as `:fastest` may choose a different inference provider without changing the base model ID, so Ax does not attach one provider's reasoning contract to that dynamic route.

candidate_sections.heading: ## AWS Bedrock
### Anthropic Model-Specific Behavior
candidate_sections.text:
### Anthropic Model-Specific Behavior

- Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, 4.7, and 4.6 plus Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5:
  adaptive thinking, no manual `budget_tokens`, and no `temperature` / `topP` /
  `topK`. When thoughts are requested, Ax asks Anthropic for summarized
  display; when they are hidden, Ax explicitly requests `display: 'omitted'`.
- Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5 always think, so `thinkingTokenBudget:
  'none'` sends the lowest effort with thoughts hidden instead of disabling it.
- Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 think by default, so `'none'` sends
  `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }`. Opus 5 only allows that at effort `'high'`
  or below, so Ax rejects `'none'` combined with `'xhigh'` or `'max'`.
- Sonnet 5.5 uses `thinking: { type: 'between_tools' }` for `'none'`,
  allowed at effort `'high'` or below. Its signed between-tool updates are
  retained in `thoughtBlocks` for replay even when display thoughts are hidden.
  Streaming and non-streaming responses preserve both thinking and redacted
  blocks; `showThoughts: false` suppresses the display `thought` field.
  The generated Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust clients share these rules,
  including effort validation, native structured output, and signed replay.
- Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1 refuse forced tool choice: Ax throws for
  `functionCall: 'required'` or a named function, and structured output uses
  the native `output_config.format` path.
- Haiku 5.5 (`AxAIAnthropicModel.Claude55Haiku`, also on Vertex):
  adaptive thinking defaults to medium effort. `'none'` sends
  `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }`; combining it with `'xhigh'` or `'max'`
  fails locally. Other thinking levels use adaptive thinking with effort.
  Forced tool choice is supported, as are native JSON Schema and function-based
  structured outputs. Empty signed thinking blocks remain available for replay;
  keep history append-only, including later system messages on both APIs.
  The context window is 1M tokens and the output limit is 128K. Per million
  tokens, input/output pricing is $0.10/$0.50 through 100K input tokens and
  $0.50/$2.50 above 100K, counting cached input toward the threshold. Cache
  reads and 5-minute writes use the corresponding tier. These semantics are
  shared with the generated Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust packages.
- Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5, and Fable 5.1 keep a later system
  message in place on the first-party API; other models hoist it into the
  system prompt. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 preserve later system messages on Vertex,
  keeping the prefix before signed thinking unchanged.
- Opus 4.5: budget_tokens + effort levels (capped at `'high'`)
- Other thinking models: budget tokens only

For assistant replay, empty visible text (`content: ''`) adds no synthetic text block. Cache markers attach only to text or tool-use blocks, never to signed or redacted thinking. See the [25.4.9 replay mapper](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/3ad7b69947e05f1770b1bd6cb1316a8ec7fcd106/src/ax/ai/anthropic/api.ts#L1871-L2013).

Anthropic `modelConfig.effort` can be set directly on a request. Fast mode and task budgets are Anthropic-only opt-ins; `taskBudget.total` must be at least 20,000 tokens.

```typescript
const res = await claude.chat({
  chatPrompt: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Review this migration plan.' }],
  modelConfig: {
    effort: 'xhigh',
    speed: 'fast',
    taskBudget: { type: 'tokens', total: 64_000 },
  },
});
```

candidate_sections.heading: ## Rules
candidate_sections.text:
## Rules

- Supply identity from authenticated adapter state, never from event data.
- Treat events without verified identity as anonymous and untrusted.
- Envelope `id`, `source`, and `type` must each be a primitive string containing
  a non-whitespace character. TypeScript rejects malformed fields before route
  matching or store enqueue, not as mapped-input dead letters. It validates
  without trimming or coercing accepted values. These envelope identifiers are
  distinct from authenticated `AxEventIdentity` fields such as `tenantId`;
  nonblank identifiers do not establish authority or URI validity.
- Map event data into signature inputs; do not synthesize a user message.
- Use `eventPath.data('field')` and other segment-safe selectors. Do not use
  dotted JSONPath strings or repurpose `s()` as a mapping language.
- Use `.project(path)` only for same-name signature projection. Explicit
  `.field()` mappings override projection; missing or invalid signature inputs
  dead-letter before model invocation.
- Use `eventInput().project(...).field(...)` when a declarative mapping should
  be callback-free and reusable, then pass that plan to `.input()`,
  `.wakeInput()`, or `.resumeInput()`.
- Callback `mapInput` is an escape hatch, not a validation bypass: its result is
  normalized to the program signature and mapper failures dead-letter before
  invocation.
- Use `.wakeInput()` and `.resumeInput()` when the two actions need different
  contracts. Neither action silently uses the other action's mapping.
- Use `observe` for progress/logs and `invalidate` for catalog changes.
- Use `resume` only with an owned continuation correlation key.
- Use `.createProgram(signature, factory)` for fresh, state-restorable instances of stateful multi-tenant Agents; do not share one mutable instance across tenants.
- Declare `retrySafety: 'idempotent'` only when stable delivery keys protect
  every possible side effect.
- Persist outputs before final sink delivery; redrive sink failures separately.
- Use `debounceMs` and `coalesce: 'latest'` only when replacing intermediate
  events is part of the route's declared policy.
- Observe source failures with `onSourceError`.
- The in-memory store is volatile and single-process.
- For cooperating Node processes on one local disk, use
  `AxSQLiteEventStore` from `@ax-llm/ax-tools/event/sqlite` with explicit
  retention and `coordination: 'multi-worker'`. Never recommend SQLite on a
  network filesystem.
- Close the runtime and caller-owned protocol clients explicitly.
- Fan out to several Agents with several matching routes, not a multi-target
  route. This preserves independent authorization, ordering, retries, and runs.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Minimal Pattern
## UCP Adapter
candidate_sections.text:
## UCP Adapter

Use `AxUCPWebhookEventSource({ client, identity })` inside an application-owned
HTTP handler, then call `source.ingest(request)`. The client verifies signer
profile, RFC 9421 signature, digest, freshness and key rotation before enqueue.
Resolve tenant/account identity from trusted application registration after
verification; never copy authority from the business payload.

**25.4.11 replay qualification:** `AxUCPClient.verifyOrderEvent` creates a new
signature verifier per request; its persistent process-local replay check uses
`Webhook-Id`, while that header and `Webhook-Timestamp` need not be signed.
Bind them to the signed `request-id` and `created` before ingestion, and require
the signed signer-profile header. Parse exactly one verified signature member
with unique parameters; bind metadata to that member, not a separately selected
or ambiguous `Signature-Input` entry. The
[`35-ucp/webhook-freshness-member-binding`](../examples/35-ucp.ts) case includes a
fresh `created`-last control and rejects old or ambiguous metadata before enqueue.
The [verified webhook example](../examples/35-ucp.ts) also covers real client
verification, key rotation, tamper/replay rejection and host-bound tenant routing.
Its volatile replay state is not restart durability; production hosts need
durable replay/idempotency policy. Source:
[`25.4.11 client and signing code`](https://unpkg.com/@ax-llm/ax@25.4.11/index.js.map),
embedded `../ucp/client.ts` (`verifyOrderEvent`) and `../ucp/signing.ts`.

Native UCP attachment is independent of transport. The same example carries
UCP through Flow → Agent/Gen and preserves structured results; MCP-backed UCP
also reuses protocol sessions and propagates cancellation. Attaching a client
does not itself authorize purchases or establish tenant isolation.

The generated-language statements below describe the supplied source's scope, not runtime qualification performed by this collection.

The supplied official 25.4.12 event-runtime guidance
also specifies field-specific `id`/`source`/`type` validation before routing or
enqueue in generated runtimes; Python dictionary envelope fields are not
string-coerced. This is source-only guidance, not independently exercised
generated/Python runtime parity. The TypeScript case below exercises the
released TypeScript boundary only.

Generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust packages expose the same Core-owned
single-worker event state machine plus functioning inline lifecycle dispatch,
continuations, state restoration, cancellation, persisted outputs, isolated
sink redrive, signature-aware path/input/target/route builders, and host-owned
source, sink, clock, and store boundaries. Generated targets use the host
signature plus a typed invocation callback when no common object-safe program
interface exists. Do not claim persistent multi-worker support from
`axevent.single-worker` alone.

Generated runtimes do not create worker threads. `publish()` drains work due at
`clock.now()`. Hosts use `nextDueAt()` to schedule `runDue()` for debounce,
retry, and continuation expiry; `redrive()` is due immediately. Manual clocks
make these transitions deterministic. Generated in-memory stores enforce
10,000 pending deliveries, 64 MiB queued data, 1 MiB per envelope, and a
five-second publication wait.

System and manual clock sleeps accept the generated cancellation token (Go uses
`context.Context`). Cancellation wakes the sleep without advancing a manual
clock, preserves the token's first reason, and removes its wake subscription on
both cancellation and normal completion. Repeated completed sleeps must not
retain timers, callbacks, condition registrations, or manual-clock waiters.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Integration and safety rules
candidate_sections.text:
## Integration and safety rules

- Pass clients through `mcp`, never `functions`. `toFunction()` is a lossy compatibility adapter for old applications, not native integration.
- Assign each client a stable unique `namespace`; let Ax classify/initialize it once and reuse its owning protocol state. Keep `era: 'auto'` unless policy pins a known endpoint. Explicitly close caller-owned clients.
- In TypeScript, `ping()` clears its deadline timer when the request settles; listening retry delays release their temporary abort listener when they finish or are aborted.
- Treat prompts, resources, tool results, and notifications as untrusted remote content. Preserve structured/multimodal results until provider capability mapping; do not flatten them to text.
- Apply `authorizeToolCall` before side-effecting tools. Never infer tenant/account identity from a session: event adapters require verified application-authentication identity.
- Notification callbacks enqueue or observe work; they must not call a model directly.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Apps, replay, evaluation, and testing
candidate_sections.text:
## Apps, replay, evaluation, and testing

Negotiate official extensions through capabilities. `AxMCPAppBridge` handles App resources/host messages; enforce CSP, permissions, visibility, allowed tools, and untrusted model-context policy. Never render arbitrary normal-tool HTML as an MCP App.

Wrap real transports with `AxMCPRecordingTransport` to record deterministic protocol interactions; use `AxMCPReplayTransport` for testing, optimization, and evaluation. `agent.optimize()` rejects live MCP clients by default because repeated model runs can repeat external side effects; set `mcpEvaluation: { mode: 'live' }` only deliberately. Its default MCP guard requires replay clients, not merely a transport labeled `sandbox`.

Testing checklist:
- Use deterministic local servers or replay; namespace/tool collisions must fail before model execution.
- Cover raw text, image, audio, resource-link, embedded-resource, metadata, task, and error results; catalog changes during multi-step runs; authorization denial before transport execution.
- Cover reconnect/logical resubscription; anonymous-event rejection by authenticated routes; terminal task resumption restricted to owning identity/correlation; cancellation and uncertain outcomes without duplicate side effects.
- Close clients, listening handles, runtimes, and local servers in `finally`, respecting source/runtime-before-client ordering.

 # Playbook Codegen Rules (@ax-llm/ax)
 
 Use this skill to generate context-playbook code. A playbook grows an evolving body of task knowledge and renders it into a program's context. The evolution engine (ACE — Agentic Context Engineering) is hidden behind `playbook(...)`, exactly as `optimize(...)` hides its optimizer. Prefer the `playbook(...)` concept; only reach for `AxACE` directly when the user explicitly wants the low-level engine.
 
 ## Use These Defaults

candidate_sections.heading: # Context playbooks and ACE evolution
candidate_sections.text:
# Context playbooks and ACE evolution

Source API snapshot: `@ax-llm/ax` 25.4.12. Use for `playbook()`, `AxPlaybook`, evolving context/task knowledge, ACE (Agentic Context Engineering), `agent.playbook()`, offline `evolve()`, and online `update()`. A playbook accumulates reusable knowledge rendered into program context. Prefer `playbook(...)`, which hides ACE; use `AxACE` directly only when low-level engine access is explicitly requested.

Playbooks complement offline instruction/demo tuning via [global GEPA optimization](gepa.md) and [agent optimization](agent-optimize.md); they are not best/Pareto optimization artifacts or inference-time [bestOfN/refine](refine.md). Only playbooks also learn online via `update(...)`.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Program-bound lifecycle
candidate_sections.text:
## Program-bound lifecycle

- Create `playbook(program, { studentAI, teacherAI? })` to obtain an `AxPlaybook` bound to an `AxGen`. `evolve`/`update` need its signature. Prefer `ai()`, `ax()`, and `agent()` for new code.
- Use a cheaper `studentAI` for execution and optional stronger `teacherAI` for reflection/curation.
- Offline: `await pb.evolve(examples, metric)` returns only `{ bestScore, playbook }`, never `paretoFront` or `optimizedProgram`. Keep the metric deterministic and cheap, as for GEPA.
- Online: `await pb.update({ example, prediction, feedback })` needs no metric and works without prior `evolve()`/`load()`; hydration is lazy on first use. Supply both `example` and `prediction`. `example` contains the program input fields plus any expected output; never put bare input fields at the top level.
- `pb.applyTo(program)` defaults to the bound program. It injects `## Context Playbook` into the program description and always recomposes from the original base; repeated calls do not stack blocks.
- Inspect `pb.render()` for markdown and `pb.getState()` for `{ playbook, artifact }`.
- Persist plain JSON with `pb.toJSON()`; restore into a fresh production program with `playbook(program, opts).load(snapshot)`.
- `teacherOptions` configures reflect/curate AI service calls. An `isExpensive` teacher (e.g. OpenAI `gpt-5.5-pro`) is rejected unless `teacherOptions: { useExpensiveModel: 'yes' }` is set. Generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust packages enforce the same gate and accept `teacherOptions` in option maps.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Agent-owned playbooks
candidate_sections.text:
## Agent-owned playbooks

`a.playbook({ target })` returns an `AxAgentPlaybook`: the stage `AxPlaybook` handle plus agent-level `evolve`. Target is `'actor'` (default) or `'responder'`. Use this agent-aware handle rather than a bare `playbook()` on an internal program. See [agent construction](agent.md) for construction-time attachment, and [context selection](agent-context.md) for choosing among playbooks, `contextMap`, `contextPolicy`, and recall.

The same playbook rendered into the agent prompt grows through three paths:

| Path | Contract |
|---|---|
| Continuous trust | Construction-time `playbook` option automatically harvests each run's failures; no dataset. |
| On-demand trust | `apb.update({ example, prediction, feedback })` injects online lessons into the live stage prompt. |
| Batch verified proof | `apb.evolve(dataset, options)` runs the full agent task set, mines failure clusters, and proposes one bullet per weakness. `verify` defaults on: retain a bullet only when held-in improves and held-out `validation` does not regress; otherwise restore the exact prior snapshot. `verify: false` is trust-batch. Bullets only. |

```typescript
const a = agent('ticket:string -> reply:string', { ai });
const apb = a.playbook({ target: 'actor' }); // default actor; or responder
await apb.update({ example, prediction, feedback });
const result = await apb.evolve(
  { train, validation }, // AxAgentEvalDataset
  { metric, runsPerTask: 2 }, // verify:true by default
);
```

Agent-level `evolve(dataset, options)` takes `AxAgentEvalDataset` plus options, runs the whole pipeline, and returns baseline/final held-in and held-out scores with per-bullet outcomes, not `{ bestScore }`. Do not confuse it with program-level `pb.evolve(examples, metric)`. To tune full-pipeline agent instructions and demos instead of playbook bullets, use `agent.optimize(...)` ([agent optimization](agent-optimize.md)).

 ## Validation And Assertions

candidate_sections.heading: # Reward-Based Selection and Refinement
candidate_sections.text:
# Reward-Based Selection and Refinement

Use `bestOfN(...)` to score complete outputs independently; use `refine(...)` when failed rounds should generate feedback that changes the next attempt. Covers reward functions, thresholds, native samples, serial attempts, advice, and diagnostics, not streaming selection. Source API snapshot: 25.4.12.

candidate_sections.heading: ## Validation and Assertions
candidate_sections.text:
## Validation and Assertions

Keep reward scoring separate from hard invariants:

| Mechanism | Purpose and failure behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Schema validation | Shape, types, and field-level constraints. |
| `addAssert(...)` | Whole-output hard invariants; failures feed correction text into the normal retry loop. |
| `addStreamingAssert(...)` | Partial streaming hard invariants; a failing partial field aborts the current stream attempt and feeds correction text into the normal retry loop. |

## String syntax and field types

```text
[description] input1:type, input2:type -> output1:type, output2:type
```

| Type | Syntax | TypeScript | Example |
|------|--------|-----------|---------|
| String | `:string` | `string` | `userName:string` |
| Number | `:number` | `number` | `score:number` |
| Boolean | `:boolean` | `boolean` | `isValid:boolean` |
| JSON | `:json` | `any` | `metadata:json` |
| Date | `:date` | `Date` | `birthDate:date` |
| DateTime | `:datetime` | `Date` | `timestamp:datetime` |
| DateRange | `:dateRange` | `{ start: Date; end: Date }` | `travelDates:dateRange` |
| DateTimeRange | `:datetimeRange` | `{ start: Date; end: Date }` | `meetingWindow:datetimeRange` |
| Image | `:image` | `{mimeType, data, details?}` | `photo:image` (input only) |
| Audio | `:audio` | input: `AxAudioInput`; output: `AxChatAudioOutput` | `recording:audio`, `speech:audio` |
| File | `:file` | `{mimeType, data \| fileUri, filename?}` | `document:file` (input only) |
| URL | `:url` | `string` | `website:url` |
| Code | `:code` | `string` | `pythonScript:code` |
| Class | `:class "a, b, c"` | `"a" \| "b" \| "c"` | `mood:class "happy, sad"` |
| Box | `:box` / `:box(evidence)` | `AxBox` / `AxBoxEvidence` | `photo:image -> target:box` |

```typescript

'query:string, context?:string -> answer:string'
'problem:string -> reasoning!:string, solution:string'
